title: Contributor payout run with late penalties and FX
scenario: Price accepted tasks (flat or per-minute), halve late submissions, convert each contributor's earnings to their payout currency or hold them below a minimum, and list the top contributors by task count. Test 2 checks the payout report.

verified.why_correct: The `//` looks like an integer-division slip, but rule 2 says per-minute pay is rounded down to a whole cent, and multiplying before dividing keeps it exact.

bugs.title: Elapsed hours drop whole days
bugs.symptom: test_late_submissions fails: T106 pays 1150 and T121 pays 2700 (full price) instead of 575 and 1350. T113 is 45 either way.
bugs.why: timedelta.seconds is only the seconds part after whole days are taken out. T106 (26 h) reads as 2 h and T121 (74 h) as 2 h, so neither is treated as late.
hints: T106 and T121 were submitted days after assignment. Why are they paid in full?
Look at how the elapsed time between two timestamps is computed.
probes: Why was T113 (23 h 59 m) right with and without the fix?
What does timedelta(days=3, hours=2).seconds return, and why?

bugs.title: Currency conversion truncates
bugs.symptom: test_local_currency_payouts fails: C01 gets EUR 878 instead of 879, and C04 gets INR 116339 instead of 116340. Other currencies match.
bugs.why: int() truncates. C01's 955 × 0.92 = 878.6 should round to 879, and C04's 1400 × 83.1 comes out as 116339.99999999999 in floating point, which truncates to 116339 instead of 116340.
hints: C04's payout is one rupee short. Multiply it out by hand.
Look at how a USD amount becomes a local amount.
to_local uses int(); the spec says round to nearest: round(...).
probes: Why is 1400 × 83.1 not exactly 116340 in Python?
Rule 2 floors and rule 5 rounds. How do you tell which applies where?

bugs.title: Counter.update on an id string
bugs.symptom: test_top_contributors fails: the list is [['C', 26], ['0', 22], ['1', 10]] instead of [['C06', 4], ['C02', 3], ['C04', 3]].
bugs.why: Counter.update iterates its argument, so a string like 'C06' adds one count each for 'C', '0' and '6'. The top list ends up made of characters.
hints: Look at the keys in top_contributors. Are they contributor ids?
How are tasks counted per contributor?
counts.update(cid) counts characters; use counts[task.contributor_id] += 1 (or update([cid])).
probes: Why didn't earned totals have the same problem?

context_qa.q: Where is a task's pay computed?
context_qa.a: pricing.task_pay looks up the rule for the task type in rates['task_types'], calls base_pay, then compares hours_between(assigned_at, submitted_at) with late_after_hours and applies late_factor with round() when it is larger.
A float number of hours between two datetimes, computed from the difference `end - start` in utils.py.
build_report keeps tasks whose cleaned status is 'accepted' and whose contributor_id is in the roster loaded by load_contributors.

context_qa.q: How does the min payout default work?
context_qa.a: load_contributors trims min_payout_usd_cents and uses DEFAULT_MIN_PAYOUT (1000) only if the trimmed text is empty; otherwise int() of the text, so '0' stays 0.
build_report fills a collections.Counter named counts while it loops over accepted tasks, then sorts counts.items() by (-count, id) and keeps the first three.
A dict with late_after_hours, late_factor, currency_rates (currency -> rate, GBP stored as a string) and task_types (type -> either per_task_cents or hourly_cents).
